checks.scope: Only BRIEF-6.md Part B: six families x four orientations x summer/winter = 48 files. Reference/ and approved out/ art are calibration sources only; no verdicts are assigned to other parts.
checks.prior_review: critic-r6B-0.json does not exist, so no inherited passes apply.
checks.individual_8x: All 48 files visually inspected at nearest-neighbour 8x in the six family sprite sheets, including every summer/winter orientation. Separate checker/dark/light 8x strips are saved for every file. Additional strips for the rejected sci-fi winter vertical, wasteland winter vertical and fantasy vertical were inspected to distinguish malformed snow from real beam/post details.
checks.one_cell_8x2: Every family inspected at 1x and 4x in a seeded 8-column x 2-row randomized one-cell sheet. Each of the eight family files occurs twice. No opaque tile backdrop, cell grid or unexplained contour seam appears. Arbitrary orientation adjacency in this stress sheet is not itself a road-connection defect; the valid approaches are checked separately. Supplemental randomized 8x2 crossing boards are also saved.
checks.road_and_river: All 48 inspected at 1x and 4x in valid river crossings with actual atlas road tiles and diagonal spill triangles. Each h/v deck reaches the correct two edges; each d1/d2 reaches the correct opposite corners. No transparent transverse gap or objectionable road-colour jump was found. Water is a flat test colour, not a proposed river asset.
checks.road_width: The named road atlases contain approximately 20-22px straight road strips on their 48px source cells, despite the brief saying about 12-14px. Bridge driving surfaces match those actual reference strips, with rails outside them. This is not rejected for violating an approximate width that conflicts with the named reference; arbitrarily narrowing them would break the required joins.
checks.pixel_quality: All candidates are RGBA, 48x48, with alpha values only 0 and 255. All visible pixels belong to one 8-connected component per image; no detached export specks. At 8x the source clusters are hard-edged, without a blurred resample, partial-alpha fringe or smooth antialiasing. Material texture remains subordinate to the silhouette at 1x.
checks.lighting: Rail/post top-edge accents and down/right inner shadows are compatible with the approved upper-left light at this overhead scale. No orientation requires rejection for a reversed light source. Cyan is emissive, not a directional highlight.
checks.palette_and_approved_art: All six settings compared against their approved markers, representative round-2 city/slums/industry/suburb/farmland tiles and paddies, plus summer/winter context scenes at 1x/4x. Grass and plains seasonal calibration boards put each bridge family next to approved bases and details at matched pixel scale, inspected at 1x/4x. Warm woods/stone, neutral concrete and restrained cyan do not clash with the approved palette.
checks.season_consistency: All 24 winter files contain visible changed pixels and retain the summer construction/orientation. Snow stays readable on rails and leaves the roadway open. The exception is scifi-bridge-v@winter: an accidental-looking transverse row of white dashes warrants rejection. Wasteland vertical winter was compared explicitly: its broader snow sits on a visible summer transverse end beam, so it is not the same defect.
checks.near_duplicates: No exact duplicate RGBA files. Orientations legitimately share family materials and road palettes; crossboards, red arch rails, braced steel, concrete guards, cyan metal and patched scrap remain distinct in the randomized sheets. Mirrored/rotated spans required to represent the same bridge are not rejected as duplicate content variants.
checks.tiling_bases: There are no Part B bases. Four approved summer/winter grass/plains reference bases are nevertheless saved as 3x3 tilings at 1x/4x for context; 1x tilings and crops preserving the central four-tile junction at 4x were inspected. They receive no new pass/fail verdict.
checks.not_applicable: Part B contains no mountains/peaks, crater props, ruins, cyberpunk city bases or tree crowns. A peak lattice/range, forest tree composite, egg-crate peaks, Swiss-cheese craters, classical ruins, stamped city street grid, flat orange autumn crowns and identical crowns are therefore out of scope, rather than omitted checks on an applicable asset.

family_observations.fantasy: Timber crossboards, warm posts and dark joints are readable against the quiet road-colour deck; muted gold/brown fits the fantasy markers.
family_observations.wuxia: Red lacquer rails and pale stone abutments distinguish the bridge from the dirt road; the bowed railing profile gives the horizontal/diagonal sprites an arch without a separate oval shadow or opaque water backdrop.
family_observations.jazz_age: Cool riveted/braced steel rails with small warm abutments read as a truss at cell scale; they fit the cream/steel approved buildings without competing with them.
family_observations.modern: Concrete shoulders and pale guard rails frame an asphalt-colour deck. The smoother h/v/d2 surfacing is credible bridge pavement, while d1 has more scuffing; this does not introduce a colour step at the ends.
family_observations.scifi: Dark metal, sparse bolts and thin cyan accents fit the road atlas; the cyan remains restrained beside approved sci-fi markers. The d1 diagonal has rail shadows rather than a blurred gradient.
family_observations.wasteland: Grey scrap sheets, irregular rusty patches and plank/metal side supports read as repaired construction; the rust is local, with enough grey remaining to avoid a flat orange slab.
